column3: The Hebrew report begins with “Behold”; BSB omits this attention marker.
Close to the Hebrew.
Relieving himself is expressed as “covering his feet”, and David’s men are said to be sitting; BSB says they were hiding.
The Hebrew says David arose, rather than explicitly creeping up, and calls the robe’s corner its “wing”. Doing as he wishes is expressed as what is good in his eyes.
David’s heart actively strikes him; BSB replaces this bodily image with a stricken conscience.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately describes bowing his face to the ground and prostrating himself; BSB condenses these into one bow.
David is explicitly named again, and the person speaking is singular; BSB leaves David implicit and uses plural “men”.
The Hebrew repeats “today” twice; BSB states the day once.

The corner of the robe is called its “wing” twice. The hand with no evil is singular, and the hunted life is his soul; BSB uses “hands” and replaces the soul expression with hunting him to take his life.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the ancients as the source of the proverb; BSB says only “old proverb”.
The Hebrew explicitly says “one flea”; BSB has “a flea”.
Judge and judging repeat a root, and the final verb also concerns judgment; BSB ends with the general “deliver”.
Saul is explicitly named three times; BSB names him once and ends with simply weeping aloud instead of raising his voice and weeping.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “you have reported”; BSB has “you have shown”.
The enemy is sent away on a “good way”; BSB replaces this image with going away unharmed.
The Hebrew emphatically repeats the reigning verb and uses singular “your hand”; BSB places certainty with knowing and uses plural “hands”.
The descendants are called “my seed”, and the two prohibitions are separately joined with “and”; BSB uses “or”.
Close to the Hebrew.
